gaps: Zen 5 X3D parts believed to exist but OMITTED because existence/spec could not be confirmed offline: Ryzen 5 9600X3D, Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Ryzen 9 9950X3D2. Emitting a wrong X3D record is the worst failure mode for this catalogue, so these are deferred to the harvest pipeline.
Zen 5 F-suffix desktop parts (Ryzen 5 9500F, Ryzen 7 9700F) omitted — recalled but not confidently verified.
Zen 5 desktop APUs on AM5 (a 9000G / Gorgon Point equivalent to the 8000G line) omitted entirely — no confident knowledge that a retail AM5 Zen 5 APU line shipped.
Ryzen 3 8300G (Phoenix 2, OEM) omitted — L3 configuration not confidently known.
Ryzen 3 5100 (Cezanne OEM) omitted — not confident it reached retail or OEM channels.
Bulldozer/Piledriver OEM-only SKUs omitted: FX-8140, FX-6120, FX-4150. Existence uncertain.
Athlon 3000G is included but the Athlon Gold/Silver PRO 3150G/3125GE OEM desktop parts are omitted (OEM-only, low gaming relevance, specs uncertain).
Sempron 2650/3850 (AM1 socket, Kabini) out of scope — AM1 is not in the requested socket set and the parts are not gaming-relevant.
Athlon II / Phenom II (AM3, pre-FX) out of scope per remit (FX onward).
A6-6400K, A4-series and other 2-core FM2/FM2+ APUs below A6-7400K omitted as not gaming-relevant.
pcieLanes null for Threadripper 7000/9000 non-PRO (TRX50) and for all Phoenix 8000G parts — the exact CPU-provided lane budget was not confidently known.
pcieLanes null for all AM3+ FX parts: those CPUs have no on-die PCIe; lanes come from the 990FX/970 northbridge. pcieGen 2 is recorded as a platform-level value.

MISSING iGPU RECORDS the gpu catalogue must add before these igpuId references resolve (12 refs, 38 CPU records affected): amd-radeon-graphics-raphael-2cu (the 2 CU RDNA 2 iGPU on every non-F Raphael and Granite Ridge desktop part — 20 records depend on it); amd-vega-7-renoir and amd-vega-6-renoir (4600G/4650G and 4300G/4350G); amd-radeon-hd-7660d, amd-radeon-hd-7560d, amd-radeon-hd-8670d (Trinity/Richland); amd-radeon-r7-kaveri-512sp, amd-radeon-r7-kaveri-384sp, amd-radeon-r5-kaveri-256sp (Kaveri/Godavari); amd-radeon-r7-bristol-ridge-512sp, amd-radeon-r7-bristol-ridge-384sp, amd-radeon-r5-bristol-ridge-384sp (Bristol Ridge).

The gpu-amd agent emitted only discrete desktop GPUs (0 igpu records); all AMD integrated graphics currently live in gpu-intel.json. Whichever agent owns that namespace needs to fill the 12 gaps above.

S-suffix (65W low-power) desktop SKUs are omitted across every generation. They are numerous (i7-2600S, i5-4570S, i7-8700S-class OEM parts, etc.), are near-duplicates of the 65W non-suffixed part at lower clocks, and are effectively absent from the retail gaming market. Roughly 60-80 SKUs not emitted.

T-suffix (35W) parts are only sampled, not enumerated: i7-3770T, i7-6700T, i7-7700T, i7-8700T, i9-9900T, i5-9400T, i5-10400T, i9-11900T. 12th/13th/14th gen and Arrow Lake T parts (12900T, 13900T, 14900T, 285T, 265T, 245T, 235T, 225T) are omitted because I am not confident in their individual base/boost clocks. Roughly 40 SKUs not emitted.

OEM-only / tray-only SKUs are omitted throughout (i5-8400T-class, i7-9700TE, i5-2405S, Core i5-13400T, the "Intel Processor 300/300T" Raptor Lake entry part, and the 65W OEM 12900/13900 variants already partly covered).

Celeron desktop parts are almost entirely omitted per the gaming-relevance filter. Only Celeron G6900 (Alder Lake) is included. Sandy through Comet Lake Celerons (G530, G1610, G1840, G3900, G3930, G4900, G5900) are not emitted.
Sandy Bridge and Ivy Bridge Pentium parts (G620, G840, G850, G860, G2020, G2120, G2130) are omitted: dual-core, no HT, no AVX, not credible gaming parts even in 2012.
Xeon parts excluded by remit, including the LGA1151/LGA1200 Xeon E-series that share silicon with the desktop i7 parts and were used in budget builds.
Mobile parts excluded by remit.
Alder Lake-N / Twin Lake (N100, N305) are omitted: BGA-only, not socketed desktop parts.
Core Ultra 200S T-variants and any 200S refresh SKUs launched after my knowledge cutoff are not represented.
No record has cpuWeightOverride: per-game CPU weights need fixture data to fit and cannot be seeded from model knowledge without inventing numbers.
vramDemandGB covers 1080p/1440p/2160p only; 3440x1440 is left absent so the estimator interpolates from pixel count rather than reading a fabricated figure.

minVramGB is null for 4 records (Fortnite, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, Total War Warhammer III, Civilization VII) where the published minimum names a GPU family with no VRAM figure, names an iGPU, or where the published table contradicts itself.

minCores is null for 7 records and minThreads for 7 (MSFS 2024, Civilization VII, ARMA Reforger, Metro Exodus Enhanced, Spider-Man 2, Hellblade II in both; plus Counter-Strike 2 for cores, where Valve publishes only a thread floor, and Star Citizen for threads, where CIG publishes only 'quad core') rather than risk a false CORE_FLOOR/THREAD_FLOOR WILL_NOT_RUN.
minSystemRamGB is null for 1 record (The Finals).

minShaderModel is null for Starfield and Alan Wake 2 because their real requirements (SM 6.6, mesh shaders) cannot be expressed in this catalogue's shader-model vocabulary without falsely gating hardware the games actually run on.

Dual-GPU desktop boards omitted (HD 7990 Malta, R9 295X2, Radeon Pro Duo): representing two GPUs as one GpuRecord would feed the fitted model a shader/TFLOPS figure no game can actually use, since CrossFire is dead in modern titles.

OEM-only rebadges omitted: Radeon R7 350 / R7 340 / R5 340X / R5 330 / R5 240, the entire RX 500X series (RX 550X/560X/570X/580X), RX 5300, OEM RX 5500 and RX 5600, RX 6300, RX 640/630. These were never sold at retail as standalone cards.
Pre-GCN VLIW parts sold under HD 7000 marketing names (HD 7670, HD 7570, HD 7510, HD 7450) omitted: they are TeraScale rebrands, outside the GCN 1.0+ remit.

China/regional SKUs omitted for lack of confident clocks: RX 6750 GRE 12GB and 10GB, RX 7650 GRE, RX 580 2048SP, RX 470D, RX 560D, and the non-XT RX 9060. Each is a real product; I could not recall boost clocks to within the 8% fp32 consistency band and would not guess.
RX 5700 XT 50th Anniversary Edition omitted: identical silicon to the RX 5700 XT with a 75 MHz higher boost, low value against the risk of family-ordering noise.

lengthMm and slotWidth are null on every record: both are AIB-board properties, not chip properties, and vary by 100mm+ across partners for the same SKU. The harvest pipeline should source these per board, not per SKU.
pciIds omitted entirely: pci-ids.ucw.cz and TechPowerUp are egress-blocked, and PCI device IDs are exactly the class of datum where a near-miss from memory is worse than absence.

driverEolDate is null on all records including the eol GCN 1.0-3.0 parts: I am confident about the status (AMD moved GCN 1.0-3.0 to legacy driver branches) but not about the precise announcement/final-driver dates.
Mobile and Radeon Pro / FirePro / Instinct parts excluded per remit.

No pciIds on any record. Intel/AMD PCI device ids were not emitted because I am not confident enough in specific hex ids to risk poisoning the alias resolver; scripts/parse-aliases.ts harvests them from pci.ids anyway.
No Arc B770 or any Battlemage part above B580. I could not confirm such a desktop SKU actually shipped, and the BRIEF says omit rather than invent.
No Arc Pro workstation cards (A40/A50/A60, Pro B50/B60) — professional SKUs, and I am not confident of their full specs.
No Intel Iris Xe MAX (DG1). It was an OEM-only discrete part and I am not confident of its retail desktop presence or clocks.
No Panther Lake / Xe3 integrated graphics. I cannot confirm the shipping SKU names or clocks, so the newest Intel iGPU generation is missing.
baseClockMHz is null on every record. Intel publishes no base clock for Arc; iGPU graphics base frequency varies per host CPU SKU and I did not want to pick one arbitrarily.
recommendedPsuW populated only for A750/A770 (Intel states 600W). Null for A310/A380/A580/B570/B580.

lengthMm/slotWidth/powerConnectors populated only where an Intel reference/Limited Edition design exists (A750, A770 16GB, B580). A380/A310/A580/B570 are AIB-only designs with wide variance, so those fields are null.
driverEolDate is null on every record, including the eol Gen6-Gen8 Intel parts — I know support ended but not the exact dates.
fp32TFLOPS is null for HD Graphics 2000/3000 (Gen6). Sandy Bridge EUs have no FMA, so shaders*clock*2 overstates them by 2x and emitting it would have been a knowingly wrong number.
Desktop Ryzen 8500G/8600G iGPU clocks (740M/760M at desktop power) not emitted as separate records; only the mobile Phoenix clocks are covered, plus the 8700G 780M which I am confident about.
Mobile-only Vega APU configurations (4800U/5800U-class Vega 8 at their own clocks) are not covered; only desktop APU parts.
No Intel Iris Plus 640/650/655 (Kaby Lake-R/Coffee Lake GT3e) and no UHD P630 workstation part.
No Meteor Lake-U 4 Xe-core "Intel Graphics" record — I was not confident enough in its max frequency.

Dual-GPU flagships (GTX 590, GTX 690, GTX Titan Z) deliberately omitted: one board carries two GPUs, so shaders/memBusBits/vramGB cannot be expressed in this schema without either doubling the shader count (which would make the fitted perf model wildly overestimate them, since AFR scaling is 0-70% and modern titles do not support SLI at all) or halving the marketed VRAM. Better absent than silently wrong.

OEM-only SKUs omitted for lack of confident specs: GTX 555, GTX 545, GT 545, GT 530, GT 420, GT 405, GTX 460 v2, GTX 645, GTX 660 OEM (1152-core), GTX 760 Ti (OEM), GTX 745, GT 605, GT 635, GT 705, GT 1010.

Ultra-low-end parts whose marketing name covers multiple different GPUs omitted: GT 630 (GF108 / GK107 / GK208 revisions), GT 620, GT 640 GDDR5 and GK208 revisions, GT 730 GF108 128-bit DDR3 revision. Splitting them correctly needs the PCI-ID tables that are egress-blocked here.
Regional/market variants omitted: GTX 1060 5GB (China), RTX 4090 D, RTX 5090 D, RTX 4070 GDDR6 (2024 respin), RTX 3050 8GB GA107 115W respin.

No RTX 50 "Super" refresh parts are included. As of this seed I have no reliable shader/clock/VRAM figures for any 2026 Blackwell refresh, and the brief forbids guessing. If such parts shipped, they are missing.
pciIds is absent on every record - PCI device IDs come from driver INF tables (pci-ids / TechPowerUp), both egress-blocked. The alias resolver gets nothing from this seed.
lengthMm is null on ~80% of records. Only Founders Edition / reference lengths I am confident of are populated; AIB board length variance is 40-80mm and guessing it would be worse than a null.
driverEolDate is populated only for Fermi and Kepler. Maxwell/Pascal/Volta moved to legacy after the seed cutoff and I am not confident of the exact branch end date.
fp32TFLOPS is null on all 17 Fermi records - see uncertainties, the shader hot clock is not representable in this schema.

AIB-only double-VRAM variants below Kepler are not split out (GTX 460 2GB, GTX 560 Ti 2GB, GTX 650 Ti 2GB, GTX 750 Ti 1GB). Kepler-era splits that Nvidia listed itself (680/670/660 Ti/660/770/780) are included.
Mobile parts, Quadro/Tesla/workstation parts and all pre-Fermi GeForce (GT200 and older) are out of remit and absent by design.
